title: Fetal biophysical profile
what: On ultrasound, the doctor checks how your baby breathes, moves, and holds muscle tone, and how much amniotic fluid there is. A heart rate trace, called CTG, is often done too.
why: Usually in the third trimester, when the baby's well-being needs checking, for example if you are past your due date or the baby is moving less.
duration: usually 30 to 40 minutes; the result is given right away
tell_doctor: If the baby is moving less
If you have leaking fluid or bloody discharge
If you have high blood pressure or diabetes

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: It is better to eat before the scan. A hungry baby can be sluggish. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Watching can take up to half an hour, because the baby may be asleep. Be patient.

steps: You lie on the exam table, and gel is put on your belly
The doctor watches the baby on ultrasound
The doctor looks for breathing movements and movements of the body and arms
The amount of amniotic fluid is measured
If ordered, CTG sensors are put on your belly to record the baby's heartbeat
feel: Lying on your back can be uncomfortable. You can ask to turn on your side
after: The doctor tells you the score right away
If the score is low, the test may be repeated or the timing of birth discussed. Your doctor decides
At home, keep track of your baby's movements
red_flags: The baby has almost stopped moving: go to the maternity hospital right away
Leaking fluid or bleeding: call emergency services
Severe belly pain or regular contractions

faq.q: Why wasn't the baby moving on the ultrasound?
faq.a: The baby may have been asleep. Usually the doctor just waits or asks you to change position.
Usually it is a good result. Your doctor will explain it for your situation.

reminders.text: Fetal biophysical profile tomorrow. Eat before the visit and bring your pregnancy record card.
